pr_title: Allow absence of `hostname` command by adding BaseStrategy
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Current workings of the hostname module lets it fail if the
command `hostname` is absent on the environment. This is because
`GenericStrategy` is also the base to be inherited by all the other
strategies. Split off `BaseStrategy` and make all the other strat.
inherit from it.

Fixes #74556

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
hostname

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
pr_comments:
The test `ansible-test sanity --test pep8` [[explain](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/dev_guide/testing/sanity/pep8.html)] failed with 2 errors:
```
lib/ansible/modules/hostname.py:227:1: E302: expected 2 blank lines, found 1
lib/ansible/modules/hostname.py:236:1: E302: expected 2 blank lines, found 1
```

It is explicitly mentioned in the documentation that `hostname` is needed to execute this module:
https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/hostname_module.html#requirements. The error message from the output you provided says it as well.

You're right.
However, in the case of systemd, `hostname_cmd` is rewritten with the `hostnamectl` command. [1]
So I think it is maked to run without `hostname` command.

[1] https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/v2.11.0/lib/ansible/modules/hostname.py#L406

Have you tried specifying the Systemd strategy as documented in https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/hostname_module.html#parameter-use?
```yaml
- hostname:
    name: my_hostname
    use: systemd
```

The same is true if you run it with `use: systemd`.

```yaml
- hosts: localhost
  tasks:
    - name: set hostname
      hostname:
        name: example.com
        use: systemd
```
